title: Donald Trump learns that WikiLeaks has Clinton campaign emails
description_short: Donald Trump learns that WikiLeaks has Clinton campaign emails
description_medium: In August 2016, Roger Stone told Donald Trump and campaign officials that WikiLeaks was expected to publish emails from Hillary Clinton campaign chairman John Podesta. A Senate Intelligence Committee report later confirmed that Stone passed along the information, but could not determine how much was genuine advance knowledge or where it came from. The report also described Stone and Jerome Corsi discussing an explanation and deleting communications.
description_long:
In early August 2016, Roger Stone learned that WikiLeaks planned to release emails from John Podesta, chairman of Hillary Clinton’s campaign, and relayed that expectation to Donald Trump and campaign officials. The Senate Intelligence Committee later confirmed that the information reached Trump, Paul Manafort, Rick Gates, and likely others. Investigators could not establish how much of Stone’s information was authentic or nonpublic, or identify its source.

Jerome Corsi, whom Stone was believed to have relied on, gave conflicting accounts of whether he had received a tip or inferred that Podesta was the target. The committee described Corsi and Stone coordinating an explanation and Corsi deleting related communications. On October 7, Stone asked WikiLeaks to release the emails as a distraction from the Access Hollywood recording. The report establishes that campaign figures received advance word and that Stone sought a release; it leaves unresolved what Trump and others knew about the source and timing.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump learns that WikiLeaks has Clinton campaign emails
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump learns that WikiLeaks has Clinton campaign emails

title: Trump: REPORT: Elon Musk's political propaganda earned 17 billion views
description_short: Trump: REPORT: Elon Musk's political propaganda earned 17 billion views
description_medium: A Center for Countering Digital Hate report counted 17.1 billion views for Elon Musk’s political posts on X between his July 13, 2024 endorsement of Donald Trump and Election Day. The group said the total exceeded twice the views recorded for political campaign ads in X’s disclosure data over the same period. The comparison measures reported views, not unique viewers or the posts’ effect on votes.
description_long:
The Center for Countering Digital Hate reported that Elon Musk’s political posts on X received 17.1 billion views between his July 13, 2024 endorsement of Donald Trump and the election. The group described many of the posts as false or misleading and compared the view count with X’s disclosure data for political campaign advertisements, which recorded less than half as many views over the same period.

The comparison puts Musk’s organic posts alongside paid ads to illustrate their reported reach on the platform during a presidential campaign. A view count does not show how many distinct people saw the posts, whether they believed them, or whether the posts changed anyone’s vote. The report’s central finding is the scale of exposure it attributed to Musk’s political content in the months before the 2024 election; it does not measure persuasion or electoral impact.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: REPORT: Elon Musk's political propaganda earned 17 billion views

title: Trump: Punishing Colorado, Trump moves Space Command HQ to Alabama
description_short: Trump: Punishing Colorado, Trump moves Space Command HQ to Alabama
description_medium: Donald Trump announced on September 2, 2025, that U.S. Space Command headquarters would move from Colorado to Alabama. Colorado’s congressional delegation warned that relocation could delay readiness and cost public money; a Pentagon inspector general had also identified readiness risks. Trump criticized Colorado’s mail-voting system around the same time. The timeline interpreted the move as political retaliation, while Trump denied that political support drove the decision.
description_long:
On September 2, 2025, Donald Trump announced that U.S. Space Command headquarters would move from Colorado to Alabama. Colorado’s congressional delegation, including four Republicans, criticized the decision, warning of delays to space-defense readiness, unnecessary expense, and strategic risk. A Pentagon inspector general had previously identified readiness concerns related to relocation.

The move was expected to take three to four years, require about 1,700 personnel to relocate, and cost hundreds of millions of dollars. The report also cited an estimated long-term cost advantage of $426 million for Huntsville, a saving that would take time to realize. Trump separately attacked Colorado’s mail-voting system. The timeline characterized the relocation as punishment for Colorado’s voting record and a reward for Alabama’s support; Trump denied that political support influenced his choice. The announcement set off a dispute over strategy, cost, and motive, while leaving the practical case for the move unresolved.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Punishing Colorado, Trump moves Space Command HQ to Alabama
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Punishing Colorado, Trump moves Space Command HQ to Alabama

title: Trump: Les Wexner gives 9 East 71st Street to Jeffrey Epstein
description_short: Trump: Les Wexner gives 9 East 71st Street to Jeffrey Epstein
description_medium: Les Wexner transferred his Manhattan townhouse at 9 East 71st Street to Jeffrey Epstein in 1995 or earlier, according to the timeline; the exact date is unknown. The transfer became public in a January 1996 New York Times report. Wexner had bought the seven-story home in 1989 for $13.2 million and spent tens of millions on renovations and furnishings. Epstein later confirmed that the property was his.
description_long:
Les Wexner bought the seven-story townhouse at 9 East 71st Street in Manhattan in 1989 for $13.2 million. He later spent tens of millions of dollars on renovations, art, and furnishings. The New York Times reported in January 1996 that Jeffrey Epstein had become the owner; the timeline places the transfer in 1995 or earlier but says the exact date is unknown.

The newspaper described Epstein as Wexner’s protégé and one of his financial advisers. Asked about the house, Epstein said it was now his and that Wexner had rarely stayed there. The report described elaborate features, including a concealed reinforced bathroom and a heated sidewalk, which conveyed the scale of the residence but did not explain the legal terms of the transfer. The available account documents a major property transfer and the financial relationship between the two men. It does not connect Donald Trump to the transaction.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Les Wexner gives 9 East 71st Street to Jeffrey Epstein
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Les Wexner gives 9 East 71st Street to Jeffrey Epstein

title: Trump: Jack Posobiec and Ali Alexander announce Stop The Steal 2020
description_short: Trump: Jack Posobiec and Ali Alexander announce Stop The Steal 2020
description_medium: On September 7, 2020, Jack Posobiec posted about “Stop The Steal 2020,” while Ali Alexander told a Periscope audience he was building a digital campaign around the slogan. Alexander described a database and alert system for Trump supporters near election offices, ballot-counting sites, and court proceedings. Pro-Trump Facebook pages began using the phrase hours later, but the timeline could not establish who operated them.
description_long:
On September 7, 2020, Jack Posobiec tweeted about “Stop The Steal 2020.” Ali Alexander separately told viewers on Periscope that he was building a digital campaign to “stop the steal.” Alexander said the effort would collect information about Trump supporters and map sites in swing states where ballots were counted or election officials worked. He described collecting cellphone numbers so people within 100 miles could be alerted to locations he considered involved in improper counting or to federal court hearings. He later released a website and app for the database.

Pro-Trump Facebook pages began using “Stop The Steal” within hours, but the timeline says they may have been run by Alexander, Posobiec, or others. The posts and announcements document plans to organize supporters around election-related locations. They do not show how many people joined, whether alerts were sent, or what happened at any election office as a result.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Jack Posobiec and Ali Alexander announce Stop The Steal 2020
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Jack Posobiec and Ali Alexander announce Stop The Steal 2020

title: Trump: Miller: Trump needs Houthi strike to extort Egypt & Europe
description_short: Trump: Miller: Trump needs Houthi strike to extort Egypt & Europe
description_medium: A private Signal conversation on March 14, 2025, included White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller discussing U.S. strikes on Yemen’s Houthi movement. Miller wrote that Donald Trump had approved the strikes and argued that the United States should seek economic returns from Europe and Egypt. He also asked how a contribution could be enforced if Europe refused. The messages show a proposed rationale, not an implemented payment arrangement.
description_long:
In a private Signal conversation on March 14, 2025, White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller discussed U.S. strikes on Yemen’s Houthi movement with administration officials. Miller wrote that Donald Trump had given a “green light” and argued that the United States should make clear what it expected from Egypt and Europe in return. He asked how the administration could enforce a requirement if Europe did not pay, adding that the United States needed further economic gain after restoring freedom of navigation.

The conversation took place amid Houthi attacks on shipping in the Red Sea, which had prompted commercial and military vessels to take longer routes. Signal was not authorized for confidential government communications. Miller’s messages framed military action as potential leverage over countries that would benefit from safer passage. They document a proposal discussed inside the administration, not an adopted policy: the messages do not show that any payment deal or enforcement mechanism was put in place.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Miller: Trump needs Houthi strike to extort Egypt & Europe
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Miller: Trump needs Houthi strike to extort Egypt & Europe

title: Trump Fires All 46 U.S. Attorneys Overnight — Unprecedented Political Purge
description_short: Trump Fires All 46 U.S. Attorneys Overnight — Unprecedented Political Purge
description_medium: In March 2017, the Trump administration demanded the immediate resignation of all 46 U.S. attorneys appointed under Barack Obama. Preet Bharara, whom Trump had asked to stay, was dismissed after refusing to leave. The abrupt request came while federal investigations and prosecutions were active. Legal experts described gradual transitions as customary, prompting concern that the mass departures could disrupt law enforcement and invite political influence.
description_long:
On March 10, 2017, the Trump administration demanded the immediate resignation of all 46 U.S. attorneys appointed under Barack Obama. Preet Bharara was among them. The supplied account says Trump had personally asked Bharara to stay, but Bharara refused a White House phone call and was dismissed. The timing drew attention because federal investigations and prosecutions were ongoing.

Legal experts described gradual replacement of U.S. attorneys as the customary way for a new administration to maintain continuity in federal law enforcement. Bharara’s investigations involving Trump allies and associates added to questions about political motivation, although the episode was not adjudicated as a case of improper motive. The mass demand put pressure on the normal transition between administrations and raised concerns about continuity and prosecutorial independence. It also tested the boundary between a president’s authority to appoint prosecutors and the expectation that enforcement decisions remain free from personal or partisan direction.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Fires All 46 U.S. Attorneys Overnight — Unprecedented Political Purge
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Fires All 46 U.S. Attorneys Overnight — Unprecedented Political Purge

title: Trump: Epstein says he's working with Tesla, wants to become a minister
description_short: Trump: Epstein says he's working with Tesla, wants to become a minister
description_medium: In a 2018 interview at Jeffrey Epstein’s New York home, journalist James B. Stewart asked about reports that Epstein was helping Tesla find a chairman after an SEC investigation. Epstein claimed he had worked with Elon Musk and Tesla and discussed investment with Saudi Arabia. Musk and Tesla denied contact. Stewart’s account does not verify Epstein’s claims; he also said he could not confirm whether later dinner invitations involving Epstein took place.
description_long:
New York Times journalist James B. Stewart interviewed Jeffrey Epstein at his Manhattan home in 2018. Epstein claimed he had been working with Elon Musk and Tesla, amid reports that he was helping the company find a chairman after an SEC investigation. He told Stewart Tesla would not confirm their contact because he was “radioactive,” and said he was discussing investment with Saudi Arabia. Musk and Tesla denied ever contacting Epstein, and Stewart’s account did not independently verify Epstein’s claim.

Epstein also said he might become a minister and described how people could use him as a confidant. During the interview he made comments minimizing sex with underage girls. Stewart later received dinner invitations involving Epstein and public figures but said he could not confirm whether the dinners occurred. The account records what Epstein claimed and the denials that followed; it does not establish that he performed business work for Tesla or secured Saudi investment.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Epstein says he's working with Tesla, wants to become a minister
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Epstein says he's working with Tesla, wants to become a minister

title: Trump: House launches formal investigation into Trump Admin & the Capitol attack
description_short: Trump: House launches formal investigation into Trump Admin & the Capitol attack
description_medium: On March 25, 2021, seven House committees asked 16 federal agencies for records about the government’s preparation for and response to the January 6 Capitol attack. The requests covered the White House, Justice Department, FBI, Pentagon, National Guard, and other agencies. The inquiry followed the failure to reach bipartisan agreement on an independent commission. The letters began an investigation; they were not findings about the administration’s responsibility.
description_long:
On March 25, 2021, seven House committees sent records requests to 16 federal agencies about the government’s preparations for and response to the January 6 attack on the Capitol. The review sought communications dating back to December 1 and covered decisions made during the final weeks of the Trump administration. Requests went to the White House, National Archives, Justice Department, FBI, Pentagon, National Guard, Homeland Security, Interior Department, U.S. Park Police, and intelligence agencies, among others.

The inquiry came after Speaker Nancy Pelosi was unable to secure bipartisan cooperation for an independent commission. At the time, federal prosecutors had charged more than 300 people in connection with the breach, including some accused of conspiring to stop Electoral College certification. The committees’ letters sought information and preservation of records; they did not constitute a completed investigation or determine the administration’s responsibility. They marked an effort by Congress to reconstruct what agencies knew and did before and during the attack.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: House launches formal investigation into Trump Admin & the Capitol attack
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: House launches formal investigation into Trump Admin & the Capitol attack

title: Trump Ends Offshore Wind Leases and Terminates Clean Energy Subsidies
description_short: Trump Ends Offshore Wind Leases and Terminates Clean Energy Subsidies
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Donald Trump halted new offshore wind leasing in federal waters and directed agencies to review existing leases. He also sought to claw back clean-energy subsidies authorized by the Inflation Reduction Act. The supplied account says the directives threatened projects and jobs, and that states and companies challenged them, including on contract grounds. The orders began reviews and legal disputes; they did not immediately cancel every existing lease.
description_long:
On January 20, 2025, Donald Trump issued executive orders halting new offshore wind leasing in federal waters and directing agencies to review whether existing leases should be ended. He also sought to claw back clean-energy subsidies authorized by the Inflation Reduction Act. The directives disrupted plans in an industry whose projects depend on federal lease agreements, and the supplied account says tens of thousands of jobs were at risk.

States and companies challenged the actions, arguing that ending leases or related arrangements could violate contractual commitments. Those lawsuits put the government’s obligations at issue, but the available account does not report a final court resolution. The orders marked a shift away from federal support for offshore wind and certain clean-energy incentives. They directed agencies to review existing leases; they did not cancel every lease on the day they were issued. The policy change therefore began with new restrictions and reviews while the scope of lasting cancellations remained under dispute.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Ends Offshore Wind Leases and Terminates Clean Energy Subsidies
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Ends Offshore Wind Leases and Terminates Clean Energy Subsidies
